To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

DNAAF1 mutations are associated with complex congenital heart defects, and that DNAAF1 has an essential role in the asymmetric expression of RUVBL proteins in the left-right organizer, which is critical for heart development.

we identified DNAAF1 mutations in four families with complex congenital heart defects and that DNAAF1 mutations can cause isolated congenital heart defects in addition to the known phenotype of primary ciliary dyskinnesia.
DNAAF1 mutations can cause heterotaxy, and that DNAAF1, RUVBL1, and IFT88 are part of a complex that regulates left/right asymmetry and heart development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of DNAAF1 and its interactions with the AAA+ ATPase RUVBL in cilia and heart development.
understanding how the assembly of the ciliary dynein arm and the ciliary intra-flagellar transport (IFT) machinery is coordinated.
the identification and characterisation of the genetic and biochemical basis of congenital heart disease and primary ciliary dyskenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DNAAF1 mutations can cause heterotaxy, and the pathogenic mechanism is likely to be related to the role of DNAAF1-Ruvbl1 in the assembly and/or transport of ciliary dynein.
DNAAF1 is a cytoplamic protein, which interacts with RUVBL1, and that this interaction has a functional role in heart symmetry breaking and left-right axis determination.
DNAAF1 mutations are a novel genetic cause of isolated CHD.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

DNAAF1 links RUVBL1 to the assembly of the dynein arm complex and the cilia intraflagellar transport system, and that this complex is essential for the establishment of left-right asymmetry and cardiac development.
DNAAF1 is a cytoplamic protein required for dyenien arm assembly, and mutations in DNAAF1 can cause both PCD and isolated heterotaxy.
DNAAF1 mutations lead to PCD and CHD, and that RUVBLs and DNAAF1 are required for ciliary assembly and heart laterality.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the same gene that causes primary ciliary dyskenesia can also cause congenital heart disease, suggesting that the same pathway is important for both.
DNAAF1 mutations can cause heterotaxy, which is a rare cause of CHD.
DNAAF1 is a key regulator of heart left-right axis development.
